title: L&T Profit Rises 14% as India's Q1 Earnings Season Delivers Mixed Signals
excerpt: Larsen & Toubro and Radico Khaitan post strong growth, but Hindustan Unilever and Suzlon Energy see profit dip as geopolitical headwinds weigh on select sectors.
body:
• L&T posted a 14% rise in Q1 profit to ₹4,123 crore, with domestic execution offsetting Middle East conflict disruptions
  • Radico Khaitan's profit surged 76% to ₹230 crore as premium spirits demand drove gross margins from 43% to 49%
  • Hindustan Unilever reported its highest revenue growth in 13 quarters at 10% USG, but standalone profit dipped 3.6% to ₹2,631 crore
  • Suzlon Energy's profit fell 6% to ₹305 crore despite 23% revenue growth, as higher costs offset strong wind turbine deliveries

India's Q1 FY27 earnings season delivered a split verdict on Tuesday, with infrastructure bellwether Larsen & Toubro and liquor maker Radico Khaitan posting strong numbers while consumer giant Hindustan Unilever and wind energy firm Suzlon Energy reported profit declines despite revenue growth.

The Sensex ended the day marginally lower at 76,766, down 70 points, as investors digested a packed results calendar that also included Tata Capital, Cholamandalam Finance, Ambuja Cements, and Pfizer India.

L&T: Domestic Strength Offsets West Asia Drag

Larsen & Toubro, widely considered a bellwether for capital expenditure in the Indian economy, reported consolidated net profit of ₹4,123 crore for the June quarter, up 14 percent from ₹3,617 crore a year ago. Robust performance in the domestic market helped the engineering conglomerate absorb the impact of the ongoing US-Iran conflict, which has disrupted project timelines across the Middle East.

The result underscores a broader theme of India's infrastructure boom providing a buffer against geopolitical turbulence. L&T's order book remains healthy, and analysts expect continued momentum from government spending on roads, railways, and defence.

Radico Khaitan: Premium Spirits Drive Record Quarter

Radico Khaitan turned in the day's standout performance. The maker of Rampur Indian Single Malt, Jaisalmer Gin, and Magic Moments Vodka saw consolidated net profit jump 76 percent to ₹230 crore, with revenue rising 13 percent to ₹5,868 crore. The company said it delivered its "highest ever volume, top line and profitability" in the quarter.

Gross margins expanded sharply from 43 percent to 49 percent, driven by strong demand for premium and super-premium brands, where volumes rose nearly 36 percent. Progressive regulatory reforms in key states — notably Karnataka's shift to strength-based excise taxation — have created pricing freedom that is flowing directly to the bottom line.

"Progressive regulatory reforms in key states, an improving policy environment and the sustained shift towards premium brands are creating significant opportunities."

— Radico Khaitan, Earnings Statement

HUL: Revenue Hits 13-Quarter High, but Profit Slips

Hindustan Unilever posted its highest underlying sales growth in 13 quarters at 10 percent, driven equally by volume and price. Revenue reached ₹17,184 crore. However, standalone profit after tax dipped 3.6 percent to ₹2,631 crore, weighed down by a higher tax base compared to last year's one-off provisions.

CEO Priya Nair pointed to the "strength of our brands" and "disciplined execution" in a stable demand environment, while cautioning about navigating "the short-term dynamic environment."

Suzlon: Revenue Surges, Costs Bite

Suzlon Energy's consolidated net profit fell 6 percent to ₹305 crore despite revenue from operations growing 23 percent on the back of higher wind turbine deliveries and strong execution. The profit dip reflected rising costs and a lower deferred tax benefit compared to last year. Suzlon's shares had already fallen 10 percent in July ahead of the results.

The company's 5.9 GW order book, with 66 percent from public sector and commercial customers, suggests the demand pipeline for wind energy remains robust. But investors will be watching whether Suzlon can convert top-line momentum into earnings growth in the quarters ahead.

The Broader Picture

Across the day's results, a pattern emerged: companies with domestic-focused businesses and pricing power — L&T, Radico, Cholamandalam (profit up 46 percent), Tata Capital (profit up 76 percent) — outperformed, while those exposed to global commodity cycles or one-off tax effects lagged. Ambuja Cements saw profit plunge 37 percent to ₹504 crore on lower realisations, while Pfizer India posted a modest 6.6 percent profit rise.

For NRI investors tracking India's corporate earnings from abroad, the Q1 scorecard reinforces a familiar narrative: India's domestic consumption and infrastructure story remains intact, but global headwinds — from the West Asia conflict to input cost inflation — continue to create pockets of vulnerability. The week ahead brings results from HUL's peer Dabur, auto major Maruti Suzuki, and pharma giant Sun Pharma, which will further clarify the trajectory.
